2609.18555.title: Interpretable Patch-Based Deep Learning for Wildfire Spread Prediction from Ensemble Simulations
2609.18555.paper_summary: Wildfire spread is traditionally predicted using physics-based simulators, which are physically interpretable but whose cost increases with each additional ensemble member. We ask how well deep learning surrogates can reproduce these simulations at a fraction of this cost, training them on 10,584 fire spread simulations at 2m resolution for the Rectoret region in Catalonia, Spain. Four architectures are compared: a patch-based U-Net, a transfer-learned ResNet-50, a physics-informed network constrained by the wind-driven advection equation and a Swin-Unet transformer. Among the terrain and vegetation variables, only surface fuel load predicts burn probability with any strength (r = 0.27) and including it lowers prediction error by 21%. The remaining variables correlate weakly and are highly duplicative. Next, an experiment with saliency, occlusion and rotation demonstrates the models' learning. Convolutional models rely primarily on distance from the current fire front, while Swin-Unet assigns more weight to fuel and terrain, a finding also noted in an unrelated wildfire dataset. When applied without retraining to the second region, Pedriza, all three convolutional models still predict fire spread, losing accuracy by a small but systematic margin.
2609.18555.paper_summary_zh: 野火擴散的預測傳統上是使用基於物理的模擬器，這些模擬器具有物理可解釋性，但隨著每增加一個集成成員，其成本也會增加。我們詢問深度學習替代模型在這一成本的一小部分下能多好地重現這些模擬，並在西班牙加泰羅尼亞的Rectoret地區對10,584個火災擴散模擬進行了2米解析度的訓練。比較了四種架構：基於區塊的U-Net、轉移學習的ResNet-50、一個受風驅動平流方程約束的物理知識網絡，以及一個Swin-UnetTransformer。在地形和植被變量中，只有地表燃料負荷以任何強度預測燃燒概率（r = 0.27），並且包括它可以將預測誤差降低21%。其餘變量的相關性較弱且高度重複。接下來，通過顯著性、遮擋和旋轉的實驗展示了模型的學習。卷積模型主要依賴於與當前火災前沿的距離，而Swin-Unet則對燃料和地形賦予更多權重，這一發現也在一個無關的野火數據集中被注意到。當不經重新訓練應用於第二個地區Pedriza時，所有三個卷積模型仍然能預測火災擴散，但準確性以小但系統性的幅度下降。
